text:
Jonatan Berggren hasn't played since Nov 3, and before that his first full season in St. Louis was steady without being loud: five points in 15 games, three of them on the power play, at about 14 minutes a night.

The Blues have 50% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, slightly better than without him, and they've scored 4.4 fewer goals than those chances deserve when he's out there. His own two goals came on 2.4 expected. Nothing here is a warning sign; it's a middle-six winger getting middle-six results.

He came over from Detroit, which took him 33rd in 2018, after 64 points in 70 AHL games for Grand Rapids. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting 1.8 shots per 60 off passes across the slot or from behind the net, though from only nine tracked games. Our projection sees about 13 goals if he plays the rest of the way. We'd like to know why he's been out before guessing more.
